name: assert_fact
description: Assert a clinical fact into Lisa's working memory. Each fact has a type (e.g. gram, morphology) and a value. The bridge automatically files each fact under the correct context in the patient -> culture -> organism tree; you only name an organism (via 'entity') when a case involves more than one. Use this to build up the clinical picture before running inference.

fact_type.description: The type of clinical fact to assert.

value.description: The value for this fact. Valid values depend on fact_type. Organism-level morphology/staining: gram=(pos|neg), morphology=(rod|coccus), aerobicity=(aerobic|anaerobic), growth-conformation=(clumps|chains). Enterobacteriaceae species discriminators: lactose=(fermenter|non-fermenter), indole=(positive|negative), motility=(motile|non-motile|swarming), urease=(positive|negative), pigment=(red|none). Gram-positive coccus discriminators: catalase=(positive|negative), coagulase=(positive|negative), hemolysis=(alpha|beta|gamma), optochin=(sensitive|resistant), bacitracin=(sensitive|resistant), novobiocin=(sensitive|resistant), bile-esculin=(positive|negative), salt-tolerance=(tolerant|intolerant), arabinose=(fermenter|non-fermenter), sorbitol=(fermenter|non-fermenter). Culture-level: culture-site=(blood), culture-age=(integer as string). Patient-level: burn=(serious), compromised-host=(t), hospital-acquired=(t), recent-travel=(tropical), white-blood-count=(low), infection-site=(respiratory|abdominal|urinary), neutropenia=(t), prosthetic-material=(t), iv-drug-use=(t), age-group=(neonate|infant|adult|elderly).

entity.description: Optional organism identifier (e.g. 'organism-1', 'organism-2'), used ONLY for organism-level facts (gram, morphology, aerobicity, growth-conformation, and every biochemical/disc discriminator: lactose, indole, motility, urease, pigment, catalase, coagulase, hemolysis, optochin, bacitracin, novobiocin, bile-esculin, salt-tolerance, arabinose, sorbitol) when a case has more than one organism, to keep each organism's evidence separate. Omit for single-organism cases (defaults to 'organism-1'). Ignored for patient-level facts (burn, compromised-host, hospital-acquired, recent-travel, infection-site, white-blood-count, neutropenia, prosthetic-material, iv-drug-use, age-group) and culture-level facts (culture-site, culture-age), which the bridge scopes automatically.

confidence.description: Confidence in this fact, from 0.0 to 1.0. Omit for full confidence (1.0). Use when the clinical evidence is uncertain (e.g. 'probably gram-positive' → 0.8).

name: run_inference
description: Trigger Lisa's forward-chaining inference engine. This fires all applicable rules against the current working memory and produces diagnostic conclusions with belief factors. Call this after asserting all available clinical facts.

name: get_conclusions
description: Retrieve diagnostic conclusions from the last inference run. Returns organism identities with their belief factors. Under certainty-factor mode, each belief is a single number in [-1, 1]. Under Dempster-Shafer mode, each belief is an object {bel, pl, ignorance} where bel is the lower bound of support, pl is the plausibility (upper bound), and ignorance is the width of the uncertainty interval (pl - bel). The response also includes a top-level belief_system field naming the active algebra.

name: get_rule_trace
description: Retrieve the rule trace from the last inference run. Shows which rules fired and in what order, providing an audit trail for the diagnostic reasoning. Use this to explain the reasoning behind conclusions.

name: explain_conclusion
description: Retrieve the AUTHORITATIVE, engine-recorded derivation of a concluded organism's belief — how the number was actually built, and on what published authority. Returns, for the named organism identity, each rule firing that contributed (with that rule's own belief), the premises it matched (a derived premise such as the enterobacteriaceae organism-class carries its OWN nested derivation, so the multi-hop chain is included), the belief before/after each firing, a plain-language `composition` of the arithmetic (e.g. "0.800 (organism-class enterobacteriaceae) composed with the 0.500 rule = 0.400"), and each rule's `provenance`: its `origin` (paip-subset | neomycin-extrapolation), verified literature `evidence` (e.g. NCBI Bookshelf / CDC citations), and a `belief_basis`. Call this whenever the clinician asks WHY or HOW you reached a conclusion, or BEFORE you cite a belief figure or a source — then QUOTE the returned composition and evidence. Do NOT reconstruct the arithmetic or recall citations from memory; this endpoint is the ground truth. Requires that inference has already concluded the organism (run get_conclusions first). IMPORTANT: `belief_basis` is 'illustrative' — the certainty NUMBER is a schematic teaching value, while `evidence` verifies the clinical ASSOCIATION; never present the number itself as sourced.

organism.description: The organism identity to explain, exactly as it appears in get_conclusions (e.g. 'klebsiella', 'e-coli', 'pseudomonas', 'serratia'). Must be a conclusion currently in working memory.

name: get_partial_matches
description: Check which rules have some but not all conditions satisfied by current working memory. Returns rules that are 'close to firing' — showing which conditions are already met and which facts are still needed. Use this to determine what questions to ask the clinician next.

name: reset_session
description: Clear all facts from working memory and reset the session. Optionally switch the active belief system as part of the reset. Use this when starting a new patient case or when the clinician wants to start over.

belief_system.description: Optional: switch the active belief system on this reset. 'cf' = certainty factors (Shortliffe-Buchanan); 'ds' = simplified Dempster-Shafer. Omit to keep the current setting.

name: recommend_therapy
description: Ask the deterministic therapy solver for an antimicrobial regimen covering the organisms currently identified in working memory. Call this ONLY after inference has produced organism conclusions (run get_conclusions first). The solver — not you — chooses the drugs: it runs a greedy weighted set cover that picks the fewest drugs covering every organism whose identification belief clears the coverage threshold, applies patient contraindications, and reports anything it cannot cover. You NEVER pick, add, or substitute a drug; your job is only to relay the patient's contraindications and narrate the regimen the solver returns, citing coverage, doses, and exclusions. NOT FOR CLINICAL USE — the pharmacology knowledge base is schematic and illustrative.

patient.description: Patient-state tokens that trigger drug contraindications. Include every one the clinician has stated (e.g. a penicillin allergy → 'allergy-penicillin'; pregnancy → 'pregnancy'). Omit or pass an empty array when there are no contraindications. Only listed tokens are honored; anything else is ignored by the solver.

solver.description: Which solver to use. Defaults to 'greedy' (the weighted set-cover solver). Omit unless the clinician explicitly asks for a different solver.

gate.description: Coverage-gate policy for belief-valued (interval) susceptibilities — a stewardship dial. 'belief' (default) is conservative: an agent covers only if the LOWER bound of its susceptibility interval clears the threshold. 'plausibility' is optimistic: it covers unless there is evidence against (uses the upper bound). 'midpoint' splits the difference. Omit for the conservative default; pass a different value only if the clinician wants to explore how the regimen changes under optimistic vs conservative stewardship. The response echoes the gate used.
